**User**
keep exploring the channel overview page more and find more bugs, I am pasting the entire user story for the channel overview page below. Also remember I want to see each and every tests being performed in the browser window so do it in "--headed" mode.


As a Trade Promotion Manager / Executive User,

I want to analyse key channel-level KPIs including Channel Insights, Total Channels, Total Spend, Average Channel ROI, and Incremental Revenue

so that I can understand channel performance, evaluate trade investment efficiency across channels, identify margin risks, and optimize channel-level promotion strategy.

KPIs covered in this sprint (sprint-26-6):
Tota Spend
Average Channel ROI
Incremental Revenue 
Objective of Channel Overview KPI Module
When a user clicks any of the following KPI cards from the KPI Navigator:

• Channel Insights
• Total Channels
• Total Spend
• Average Channel ROI
• Incremental Revenue

the system should open a dedicated KPI analysis module containing:

Two tabs:

• Intelligence
• Channels

The page should allow the user to:

• Analyze KPI performance through insights and visual analytics
• Compare channel performance across ROI, revenue, and efficiency metrics
• Identify structural risks such as margin erosion or overspending
• Evaluate promotion intensity across channels
• Drill down into channel-level performance details

KPI Navigator (Left Panel)
The left panel contains KPI cards which act as the primary navigation for the Channel Overview module.

Each KPI card displays a high-level metric value, and clicking on it updates the main content area with the corresponding KPI analysis.

KPIs included in this story
Channel Insights

Displays the total number of AI-generated insights related to channel performance and structural risks.

Total Channels

Displays the total number of sales channels currently included in the portfolio.

Total Spend

Displays the total promotional spend allocated across all channels.

Average Channel ROI

Displays the average return on investment generated across all channels.

Incremental Revenue

Displays the total incremental revenue generated by promotions across all channels.

Selecting any KPI loads:

• KPI-related insights
• KPI-related charts
• Channel performance summaries

SECTION 1 — COMMON FILTER BAR (Applies to Entire Module)
Filters remain consistent across all KPI views and tabs.

Filters apply to:

• Intelligence Tab
• Channels Tab
• Channel performance analysis

Required Filters
Time Period

Custom Date Range Selector

Time Aggregation

• Monthly
• Quarterly

Brand

Example values:

• AquaPure
• CleanEdge
• FreshBite
• NutriGo
• SnackWell

Region

Example values:

• Midwest
• Northeast
• South
• Southeast
• West

ROI Band

• All
• High (≥2x)
• Medium (1–2x)
• Low (<1x)

SECTION 2 — INTELLIGENCE TAB
The Intelligence tab provides AI-generated insights and visual analytics related to channel performance.

This tab helps users quickly identify:

• Channel efficiency
• Margin risks
• Discount strategy issues
• Allocation imbalances
• Forecast reliability issues

The insights are presented as Insight Cards.

Examples include:

• ROI concentration risk
• Margin destruction risk
• Forecast reliability issues
• Promotion intensity risk

Users can click “View All Channel Insights” to see the complete insight list.

Charts Section (Intelligence Tab)
All four KPIs (Total Channels, Total Spend, Average Channel ROI, Incremental Revenue) share the same chart set

Chart 1 — Channel ROI Over Time
Chart Type

Multi-line Time Series Chart

What it shows

How ROI performance for each channel evolves over time.

Each line represents a channel.

X-axis

Time Period 

Y-axis

Average Channel ROI (x)

Lines

• E-commerce
• Grocery
• Club
• Drug

Business Interpretation

Helps identify:

• Channels with improving ROI
• Declining channel efficiency
• Seasonal ROI patterns

Example insight:

If E-commerce ROI spikes in mid-year, promotions in that channel may perform better during that period.

Chart 2 — Structural Strength Radar
Chart Type

Radar Chart

What it shows

A multi-metric structural comparison of channels across five dimensions:

• ROI
• Incremental Revenue
• Efficiency
• Margin
• Forecast Accuracy

Axes

The radar chart uses five axes:

ROI

Incremental Revenue

Efficiency

Margin

Forecast Accuracy

Values

Scores normalized on a 0–100 scale.

Legend

Each colored line represents a channel:

• E-commerce
• Grocery
• Club
• Drug

Business Interpretation

Helps identify structural strengths and weaknesses.

Example insights:

• E-commerce may lead in ROI and revenue
• Grocery may perform well in efficiency
• Drug may have weaker forecast accuracy

Chart 3 — ROI Elasticity by Discount Band
Chart Type

Line Chart

What it shows

How ROI changes as discount depth increases for each channel.

X-axis

Discount Band (%)

Y-axis

Average ROI (x)

Lines

Each line represents a channel:

• E-commerce
• Grocery
• Club
• Drug

Business Interpretation

Helps determine:

• Optimal discount depth
• Over-discounting risks
• Channel pricing sensitivity

Example insight:

If ROI declines sharply beyond 30% discount, deeper discounts may destroy profitability.

Chart 4 — Allocation: Spend vs Revenue Share
Chart Type

Combined Bar + Line Chart

What it shows

Comparison of spend allocation vs revenue contribution across channels.

X-axis

Channel

Left Y-axis

Spend Share (%)

Right Y-axis

Revenue Share (%)

Elements

Bars → Spend Share
Line → Revenue Share

Business Interpretation

Helps identify whether channels are overfunded or underfunded.

Example insights:

• If spend share > revenue share → overinvestment risk
• If revenue share > spend share → growth opportunity

Chart 5 — Risk Alert Panel
Chart Type

Alert / Risk Cards

What it shows

Rule-based structural alerts highlighting channel risks.

Examples:

• Margin destruction risk
• Over-discounting
• Inefficient trade spend

Business Interpretation

Helps users quickly detect channels requiring immediate action.

Example:

If Club channel shows margin destruction risk, discount strategy may need adjustment.

SECTION 3 — CHANNELS TAB
The Channels tab displays channel-level performance data corresponding to the selected KPI.

Users can:

• Compare channels across multiple metrics
• Identify efficient channels
• Drill down into channel-level analysis

Users can switch between two views:

• Grid View
• Card View

A search bar allows users to find channels quickly.

3.1 Grid View
The Grid View displays channels in a structured table format.

Columns
Channel

Total Spend

Spend Share %

Incremental Revenue

Revenue Share %

Average ROI

ROI Gap vs Portfolio

Margin Impact

Promo Intensity %

Forecast Accuracy %

Spend Efficiency

Actions

Actions
Details → Opens Channel Details Page

The grid supports:

• Sorting
• Searching
• Comparison across channels

3.2 Card View
The Card View displays channels as summary cards.

Each card contains:

• Channel Name
• Total Spend
• Incremental Revenue
• Average ROI
• Margin Impact
• Promotion Intensity
• Forecast Accuracy

Cards also display risk tags, such as:

• Margin Risk
• Volatile
• Low Forecast Reliability

Action available:

View Channel Details

Channel Details Page
When the user clicks View Channel Details, a Channel Details page opens.

The structure of this page is the same for all channels, while the data shown is specific to the selected channel.

The page typically contains:

• Channel strategy summary metrics
• Discount elasticity diagnostics
• Brand performance within the channel
• Seasonal uplift patterns
• AI-generated optimization recommendations
• Simulation capabilities for strategy testing

This allows users to analyze channel strategy in depth and optimize trade promotion investments.

Out of Scope-KPIs
1) Speed efficiency
2)Avg Margin Impact
3)Promo Intensity
4)Forecast Accuracy
Data Source
The dashboard retrieves data from the Gold Layer – Channel Performance Fact Tables.

Typical fields include:

• channel
• brand
• region
• trade_spend
• baseline_sales
• incremental_revenue
• discount_percent
• margin_percent
• promotion_count
• forecast_accuracy
• time_period

Derived metrics such as ROI, spend efficiency, margin impact, and promo intensity are calculated in the data layer.

**User**
keep exploring the channel overview page more and find more bugs, I am pasting the entire user story for the channel overview page below. Also remember I want to see each and every tests being performed in the browser window so do it in "--headed" mode. Below is the user story:


As a Trade Promotion Manager / Executive User,

I want to analyse key channel-level KPIs including Channel Insights, Total Channels, Total Spend, Average Channel ROI, and Incremental Revenue

so that I can understand channel performance, evaluate trade investment efficiency across channels, identify margin risks, and optimize channel-level promotion strategy.

KPIs covered in this sprint (sprint-26-6):
Tota Spend
Average Channel ROI
Incremental Revenue 
Objective of Channel Overview KPI Module
When a user clicks any of the following KPI cards from the KPI Navigator:

• Channel Insights
• Total Channels
• Total Spend
• Average Channel ROI
• Incremental Revenue

the system should open a dedicated KPI analysis module containing:

Two tabs:

• Intelligence
• Channels

The page should allow the user to:

• Analyze KPI performance through insights and visual analytics
• Compare channel performance across ROI, revenue, and efficiency metrics
• Identify structural risks such as margin erosion or overspending
• Evaluate promotion intensity across channels
• Drill down into channel-level performance details

KPI Navigator (Left Panel)
The left panel contains KPI cards which act as the primary navigation for the Channel Overview module.

Each KPI card displays a high-level metric value, and clicking on it updates the main content area with the corresponding KPI analysis.

KPIs included in this story
Channel Insights

Displays the total number of AI-generated insights related to channel performance and structural risks.

Total Channels

Displays the total number of sales channels currently included in the portfolio.

Total Spend

Displays the total promotional spend allocated across all channels.

Average Channel ROI

Displays the average return on investment generated across all channels.

Incremental Revenue

Displays the total incremental revenue generated by promotions across all channels.

Selecting any KPI loads:

• KPI-related insights
• KPI-related charts
• Channel performance summaries

SECTION 1 — COMMON FILTER BAR (Applies to Entire Module)
Filters remain consistent across all KPI views and tabs.

Filters apply to:

• Intelligence Tab
• Channels Tab
• Channel performance analysis

Required Filters
Time Period

Custom Date Range Selector

Time Aggregation

• Monthly
• Quarterly

Brand

Example values:

• AquaPure
• CleanEdge
• FreshBite
• NutriGo
• SnackWell

Region

Example values:

• Midwest
• Northeast
• South
• Southeast
• West

ROI Band

• All
• High (≥2x)
• Medium (1–2x)
• Low (<1x)

SECTION 2 — INTELLIGENCE TAB
The Intelligence tab provides AI-generated insights and visual analytics related to channel performance.

This tab helps users quickly identify:

• Channel efficiency
• Margin risks
• Discount strategy issues
• Allocation imbalances
• Forecast reliability issues

The insights are presented as Insight Cards.

Examples include:

• ROI concentration risk
• Margin destruction risk
• Forecast reliability issues
• Promotion intensity risk

Users can click “View All Channel Insights” to see the complete insight list.

Charts Section (Intelligence Tab)
All four KPIs (Total Channels, Total Spend, Average Channel ROI, Incremental Revenue) share the same chart set

Chart 1 — Channel ROI Over Time
Chart Type

Multi-line Time Series Chart

What it shows

How ROI performance for each channel evolves over time.

Each line represents a channel.

X-axis

Time Period 

Y-axis

Average Channel ROI (x)

Lines

• E-commerce
• Grocery
• Club
• Drug

Business Interpretation

Helps identify:

• Channels with improving ROI
• Declining channel efficiency
• Seasonal ROI patterns

Example insight:

If E-commerce ROI spikes in mid-year, promotions in that channel may perform better during that period.

Chart 2 — Structural Strength Radar
Chart Type

Radar Chart

What it shows

A multi-metric structural comparison of channels across five dimensions:

• ROI
• Incremental Revenue
• Efficiency
• Margin
• Forecast Accuracy

Axes

The radar chart uses five axes:

ROI

Incremental Revenue

Efficiency

Margin

Forecast Accuracy

Values

Scores normalized on a 0–100 scale.

Legend

Each colored line represents a channel:

• E-commerce
• Grocery
• Club
• Drug

Business Interpretation

Helps identify structural strengths and weaknesses.

Example insights:

• E-commerce may lead in ROI and revenue
• Grocery may perform well in efficiency
• Drug may have weaker forecast accuracy

Chart 3 — ROI Elasticity by Discount Band
Chart Type

Line Chart

What it shows

How ROI changes as discount depth increases for each channel.

X-axis

Discount Band (%)

Y-axis

Average ROI (x)

Lines

Each line represents a channel:

• E-commerce
• Grocery
• Club
• Drug

Business Interpretation

Helps determine:

• Optimal discount depth
• Over-discounting risks
• Channel pricing sensitivity

Example insight:

If ROI declines sharply beyond 30% discount, deeper discounts may destroy profitability.

Chart 4 — Allocation: Spend vs Revenue Share
Chart Type

Combined Bar + Line Chart

What it shows

Comparison of spend allocation vs revenue contribution across channels.

X-axis

Channel

Left Y-axis

Spend Share (%)

Right Y-axis

Revenue Share (%)

Elements

Bars → Spend Share
Line → Revenue Share

Business Interpretation

Helps identify whether channels are overfunded or underfunded.

Example insights:

• If spend share > revenue share → overinvestment risk
• If revenue share > spend share → growth opportunity

Chart 5 — Risk Alert Panel
Chart Type

Alert / Risk Cards

What it shows

Rule-based structural alerts highlighting channel risks.

Examples:

• Margin destruction risk
• Over-discounting
• Inefficient trade spend

Business Interpretation

Helps users quickly detect channels requiring immediate action.

Example:

If Club channel shows margin destruction risk, discount strategy may need adjustment.

SECTION 3 — CHANNELS TAB
The Channels tab displays channel-level performance data corresponding to the selected KPI.

Users can:

• Compare channels across multiple metrics
• Identify efficient channels
• Drill down into channel-level analysis

Users can switch between two views:

• Grid View
• Card View

A search bar allows users to find channels quickly.

3.1 Grid View
The Grid View displays channels in a structured table format.

Columns
Channel

Total Spend

Spend Share %

Incremental Revenue

Revenue Share %

Average ROI

ROI Gap vs Portfolio

Margin Impact

Promo Intensity %

Forecast Accuracy %

Spend Efficiency

Actions

Actions
Details → Opens Channel Details Page

The grid supports:

• Sorting
• Searching
• Comparison across channels

3.2 Card View
The Card View displays channels as summary cards.

Each card contains:

• Channel Name
• Total Spend
• Incremental Revenue
• Average ROI
• Margin Impact
• Promotion Intensity
• Forecast Accuracy

Cards also display risk tags, such as:

• Margin Risk
• Volatile
• Low Forecast Reliability

Action available:

View Channel Details

Channel Details Page
When the user clicks View Channel Details, a Channel Details page opens.

The structure of this page is the same for all channels, while the data shown is specific to the selected channel.

The page typically contains:

• Channel strategy summary metrics
• Discount elasticity diagnostics
• Brand performance within the channel
• Seasonal uplift patterns
• AI-generated optimization recommendations
• Simulation capabilities for strategy testing

This allows users to analyze channel strategy in depth and optimize trade promotion investments.

Out of Scope-KPIs
1) Speed efficiency
2)Avg Margin Impact
3)Promo Intensity
4)Forecast Accuracy
Data Source
The dashboard retrieves data from the Gold Layer – Channel Performance Fact Tables.

Typical fields include:

• channel
• brand
• region
• trade_spend
• baseline_sales
• incremental_revenue
• discount_percent
• margin_percent
• promotion_count
• forecast_accuracy
• time_period

Derived metrics such as ROI, spend efficiency, margin impact, and promo intensity are calculated in the data layer.

**User**
Below is the user story for the Promo Overview page remember:

As a Trade Promotion Manager / Executive User,

I want to analyze key promotion KPIs including Promo Insights, Total Active Promos, Total Promo Spend, and Average Promo ROI

so that I can monitor portfolio performance, understand spend allocation, evaluate promotion efficiency, and identify optimization opportunities across promotions.

Objective of Promo Overview KPI Module
When a user clicks any of the following KPI cards from the KPI Navigator:

Promo Insights

Total Active Promos

Total Promo Spend

Average Promo ROI

the system should open a dedicated KPI analysis module containing:

Two tabs:

Intelligence

Promos

The page should allow the user to:

Analyze KPI performance through insights and visual summaries

Explore promotion-level performance

Compare performance across brands, channels, and time periods

Drill down into promotion-level data

KPI Navigator (Left Panel)
The left panel contains KPI cards which act as the primary navigation for the Promo Overview module.

Each KPI card displays a high-level metric value and clicking on it updates the main content area with the corresponding KPI analysis.

KPIs included in this story:

Promo Insights
Displays the total number of insights generated across promotion KPIs.

Total Active Promos
Displays the total number of promotions currently active within the selected filters.

Total Promo Spend
Displays the total trade spend allocated across promotions.

Average Promo ROI
Displays the average return on investment across promotions.

Selecting any KPI loads:

KPI-specific insights

KPI-related charts

The promotion list filtered for the selected KPI

SECTION 1 – COMMON FILTER BAR (Applies to Entire Module)
Filters remain consistent across all KPI views and tabs.

SECTION 2 – INTELLIGENCE TAB
The Intelligence tab provides AI-generated insights and visual analytics related to the selected KPI.

The goal of this tab is to help business users quickly identify patterns, risks, and optimization opportunities.

1)Promo Insights KPI
This KPI shows AI-generated insights across all promotion KPIs.
The insights summarize patterns detected in the data such as efficiency issues, risks, and optimization opportunities.

Charts / Visualization
Promo Insights itself does not have dedicated charts.

Instead it displays Insight Cards.

Users can also click “View all insights” to explore the full list of insights related to the KPI.

2)Total Active Promos KPI
This KPI shows how many promotions are currently active and how they are distributed across the portfolio.

Chart 1 — Promo Count by Brand
What it shows
A bar chart displaying the number of promotions run by each brand.

X-axis

Number of promotions

Y-axis

Brand names

Business Interpretation
This chart helps answer:

Which brand is running the most promotions

Whether promo volume is balanced across brands

If one brand is over-promoting

Example insight:
If SnackWell has significantly more promos, it may indicate:

aggressive promotion strategy
or

risk of promotion fatigue

Chart 2 — Promo Distribution by Channel
What it shows
A donut chart displaying the share of promotions by channel.

Example channels:

Club

Drug

Grocery

E-commerce

Business Interpretation
Helps understand where promotions are being executed.

Example insight:

If Drug channel has 28% of promos, execution workload may be high there.

If E-commerce is low, digital promotion opportunities may be underutilized.

This helps balance promotion distribution across channels.

Chart 3 — Weekly Promo Density Heatmap
What it shows
A heatmap showing number of promotions executed each week.

Each cell represents a week in the year.

Color intensity represents promo density:

Light → fewer promotions

Dark → more promotions

Business Interpretation
Helps detect:

Promo clustering

Seasonal promotion peaks

Execution pressure periods

Example insights:

Too many promotions in one week → execution overload

Long periods without promotions → missed sales opportunities

3)Total Promo Spend KPI
This KPI analyzes how trade spend is distributed and evolving over time.

Chart 1 — Spend by Promo (Top 10)
What it shows
A horizontal bar chart showing the top 10 promotions by spend.

X-axis

Spend amount

Y-axis

Promotion names

Business Interpretation
Helps identify:

Promotions consuming the largest portion of the budget

Potential overspending promotions

Example insight:

If one promotion has much higher spend than others, managers may review whether the ROI justifies the investment.

Chart 2 — Spend Trend (Planned vs Actual)
What it shows
A line chart comparing planned spend vs actual spend over time.

X-axis

Time period (Quarter or Month)

Y-axis

Spend value

Lines:

Planned Spend

Actual Spend

Business Interpretation
This chart helps detect:

Budget overspend or underspend

Execution deviations from plan

Example insights:

Actual spend consistently above planned → budget control issue

Actual spend below planned → under-utilization of promotional budgets

Chart 3 — Spend by Channel
What it shows
A bar chart showing total spend by channel.

Channels include:

Club

Drug

Grocery

E-commerce

Business Interpretation
Helps understand where marketing budget is concentrated.

Example insights:

High spend in one channel may create portfolio imbalance

Channels with low spend may represent growth opportunities

Managers can align spend allocation with ROI performance.

4)Average Promo ROI KPI
This KPI evaluates how efficiently promotional spend generates returns.

Chart 1 — ROI vs Spend (Scatter Plot)
What it shows
A scatter plot showing the relationship between spend and ROI.

Each dot represents one promotion.

X-axis

Trade Spend

Y-axis

ROI

Dots are color-coded to represent performance levels.

Business Interpretation
Helps quickly identify:

Quadrant	Meaning
High Spend + High ROI	Scale these promotions
High Spend + Low ROI	Risk — spending too much with poor returns
Low Spend + High ROI	Opportunity to invest more
Low Spend + Low ROI	Review or stop
This chart helps managers prioritize promotions for scaling or optimization.

Chart 2 — ROI Distribution
What it shows
A bar chart showing how promotions are distributed across ROI ranges.

Example bands:

<1 (loss-making)

1–1.5

1.5–2

2

X-axis

ROI band

Y-axis

Number of promotions

Business Interpretation
Helps understand the overall health of the promotion portfolio.

Example insights:

Large number of promotions below ROI 1 → portfolio inefficiency

Many promotions above ROI 2 → strong scaling opportunities

Chart 3 — ROI Trend Over Time
What it shows
A line chart showing how portfolio ROI changes over time.

X-axis

Time period (month or quarter)

Y-axis

Portfolio ROI

Business Interpretation
Helps track whether promotion efficiency is improving or declining.

Example insights:

Upward trend → promotion strategy improving

Downward trend → promotions becoming less effective

Managers can investigate why ROI changed during certain periods.


SECTION 3 – PROMOS TAB
The Promos tab displays promotion-level data corresponding to the selected KPI.

This tab allows users to analyze individual promotions and compare their performance.

Users can switch between multiple views:

Grid View

Card View

Calendar View

A search bar allows users to quickly find promotions by name.

3.1 Grid View
The grid view displays promotions in a structured table format.

Columns
Promo Name

Brand

Channel

Spend

ROI

Incremental Revenue

Discount %

Uplift %

Classification

Actions

Actions
Users can perform actions on each promotion:

Details – Opens the promotion details page

Simulate – Simulation capability (future sprint)

The table supports:

Sorting

Filtering

Searching

This view enables easy comparison of promotion performance across the portfolio.

3.2 Card View
The card view displays promotions as visual cards summarizing performance metrics.

Each promotion card includes:

Promo Name

Brand

Channel

Spend

ROI

Incremental Revenue

Uplift %

Classification Tag

Users can quickly identify top-performing or underperforming promotions using these cards.

Actions available:

View Details

Simulate (Future Sprint)

3.3 Calendar View
The calendar view provides a time-based visualization of promotions.

This helps users understand:

Promotion scheduling

Promotional overlap

Time-based campaign distribution

Data Source
The dashboard retrieves data from the Gold Layer – Promotion Fact Table.

Typical fields include:

promo_id

brand

channel

region

actual_spend

actual_sales

baseline_sales

margin %

discount %

time_period

Derived metrics such as incremental revenue and ROI are calculated within the data layer.
